70.t: White musicians studied; advice to take lessons
70.s: Jackson credits white musicians for studying hard and advises kids to learn technique so they can play with any feeling.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: And I give the white musicians a lot of credit because the white musicians really studied. He knew he had to study. He practiced a lot, he practiced a lot, where we used to go and just play. We had so much joy playing and we had so much originality and so much feeling that we didn't really, a lot…

70.s: Jackson says to study technique, develop an individual style, listen widely, learn piano and have self-respect.
70.ch: After the road: New York, the profession and advice
70.q: Well, the first thing that I would like to say to them is, the first thing is to learn the fine points of their instrument. You have to study. There's a lot of work involved to learn the technical part of your instrument so that there's nothing that you can't do with your instrument.

599.s: Asked for advice, Gates says to listen to the best live and on record and only sing what you truly love.

937.t: Advice to students: learn the basics and get out in the world
937.s: Heard says to learn the basics, then get out and make people smile and dance, rather than rely on schooling.
937.q: Well clinics don’t like to hire me because what I have to say I say in about 15-20 seconds. You learn the basics and you get out in the world. 499.s: Young players have more resources than he did; he advises picking a hero, researching styles, and mentions Radio Farm and Richard Tee's homework line.

494.t: What Barron imparts: the humanity of music
